The Department's main goal is to provide fire protection, emergency medical care, and other critical public safety services to residents and visitors in the five boroughs. FDNY members are sworn to serve and protect life and property and the Department works to continually educate the public in fire, life safety and disaster preparedness, along with enforcing public safety codes. Since its inception in 1865, FDNY has helped lead efforts to make New York the safest big city in the nation. This accomplishment requires a steadfast and daily commitment to maintaining the Department's core values. The FDNY Bureau of Enterprise Technology manages key departmental initiatives and drives data-driven decision-making. Its Data Quality unit is responsible for generating actionable insights through analysis, reporting, and visualizations. This unit also ensures accountability and transparency by compiling metrics for the Mayor's Management Report (MMR) and producing datasets for NYC Open Data. The Fire Department of the City of New York (FDNY) seeks a full-time City Research Scientist, L2 in the Data Quality Unit. With latitude for independent initiative and judgement, the Data Quality Analyst will assist the Department’s in the making evidence-based decisions. Day-to-day responsibilities focus on data quality and insight delivery. This includes rigorously performing data quality checks and anomaly detection. The Data Quality Analyst will also support the building of interactive dashboards, primarily using Tableau and modern Python frameworks (Dash/Streamlit). Other core duties include swift fulfilling of ad-hoc data requests and designing appropriate metrics to track and report on departmental performance. This position will also participate in community outreach, especially in the context of Open Data which could include responding to public inquiries, representing the Department at Open Data Events and gathering feedback from the community. This is a crucial function that connects the FDNY's internal data efforts with the public, leveraging data transparency to enhance safety and build trust.

Descricao: Develop a systematic data quality control, standardization, and visualization toolkit to support NYC DOT’s transition toward a more strategic, data-driven approach to citywide mobility analysis. Working directly with the Data Systems & Counts Management team, the College Aide will build new and modify existing workflows to ingest, clean, and validate multimodal traffic counts and third-party location-based mobility data. Where data permits, the project will focus on identifying spatial errors, automating repetitive data-cleaning pipelines, and mapping anomalies across citywide networks. Findings and data pipelines will directly shape how NYC DOT validates major data streams, tracks program performance metrics, and supports larger regional planning models to ensure transportation investments promote equitable and efficient mobility. Typical duties required: Typical duties include reviewing current Python-based data workflows and counts management platform metrics for familiarity. Then, the College Aide will assist in drafting data documentation standards and scripting automated quality control checks using Python and SQL. Additionally, manipulating large spatial datasets and cross-referencing field counts with third-party mobility matrices will be a substantial part of the project. Finally, the College Aide will translate complex data errors into actionable insights, compiling findings into maps, dashboard components, and technical presentations for the engineering and planning teams. What will the student learn from this experience? The student will gain highly marketable, hands-on experience in public-sector data science and transportation planning under the direct mentorship of data professionals. They will deeply develop their technical toolkit in Python, SQL, and GIS by tackling real-world, large-scale mobility datasets. This opportunity provides an inside look at metropolitan planning data infrastructure, allowing the student to build a portfolio piece that bridges technical data engineering with impactful urban policy that supports agency leadership.

Excellent organizational skills and a strong interest in multimodal data collection, transportation planning, and citywide mobility analysis.

Descricao: ** The I.T automation engineer Civil Service Title is non-competitive and does not require perspective candidates to be on a civil service list. *** About DEP: The NYC Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) protects public health and the environment for over 8 million New Yorkers. We provide 1.1 billion gallons of high-quality drinking water daily, manage wastewater and stormwater, and regulate air, noise, and hazardous materials pollution. With nearly 6,000 employees, DEP operates the largest municipal water and wastewater utility in the U.S. About BWT: The Bureau of Wastewater Treatment (BWT) operates and maintains critical wastewater infrastructure across all five boroughs, including 14 Wastewater Resource Recovery Facilities, over 90 pumping systems, combined sewer overflow facilities, and more. BWT is undergoing a digital transformation focused on four pillars: SCADA Support and Development, IT Support and Cybersecurity, Asset Management, and Application Development. This transformation aims to modernize operations and improve resilience, efficiency, and data-driven decision-making. The Section Chief of SCADA Development oversees the design, programming, and optimization of SCADA systems for BWT. This role includes leading a development team, establishing SCADA standards, managing project implementation, and aligning with cybersecurity, IT, and engineering requirements. The Section Chief will also maintain the BWT SCADA master plan, coordinate with stakeholders, and ensure successful integration and documentation of new systems and enhancements. Duties include but not limited to: -	Lead and manage the SCADA Development team and project execution. -	Develop and implement BWT’s SCADA Master Plan and Road Map. -	Establish and maintain SCADA standards, naming conventions, documentation, and procedures. -	Coordinate with engineering and construction teams to plan and develop SCADA/I&C/Automation projects. -	Collaborate with BIT to develop SCADA-specific cybersecurity and disaster recovery policies. -	Oversee SCADA architecture, coding standards, change management, and quality assurance. -	Plan and deploy solutions within Microsoft enterprise environments. -	Lead integration of SCADA with other platforms and enterprise systems. -	Incorporate DevOps practices and manage secure development lifecycles. -	Guide staff development and promote a collaborative team culture. -	Provide input on strategic planning, technology roadmaps, and budgets. -	Engage in professional development and represent DEP at relevant conferences.
Requisitos: 1. A baccalaureate degree in computer science, engineering or a related field from an accredited college and four years of satisfactory full-time experience related to IT automation engineering, monitoring engineering, management of infrastructure; or 2. Eight years of satisfactory full-time experience related to IT automation engineering, monitoring engineering, management of infrastructure; 3. Education and/or experience which is equivalent to "1" or "2" above.
Habilidades: -SCADA Architecture: Deep knowledge of SCADA protocols, integration, and infrastructure planning. -I&C Engineering: Experience standardizing and developing instrumentation and controls. -Cybersecurity: Understanding of ICS security, disaster recovery, and relevant standards (e.g., NIST, ISA/IEC). -Project Management: Ability to manage cross-functional teams and strategic SCADA initiatives. -DevOps & SDLC: Familiarity with version control, testing, and secure development practices. -Microsoft Technologies: Experience with Windows Server, SQL Server, AD, and Azure environments. -Asset & Config Management: Proficiency with Maximo, Infor EAM, or similar systems. -Automation Logic: Experience developing and troubleshooting PLCs, HMIs, and RTUs. -Data Analytics: Ability to leverage SCADA data for operational performance and insights. -Documentation: Strong technical writing and standard development skills. ***Additional Requirements*** A valid New York State driver’s license is required and must be maintained for the duration of your employment.

The individual will develop staffing plans to ensure coverage during normal and peak operational periods. The 12 hour/day work schedule will be Mon-Wed or Thu-Sat (alternate week) (with a start time of no later than 19:30 until 8 am) to allow for review of turnover from the night shift. interface with application infrastructure teams on the development of tape pull list reports; Vendor Management • Serve as a point of contact for auto-mailer (inserter), printer, pre/post print equipment, GRM vendors for their shift • Work with (above) vendors to develop quotes for standard work (moves, minor hardware, etc.); ensure that local technicians are available for service calls and are qualified (capable) to perform work; instruct vendors to store replacement parts onsite in secure lockers (based on useful life and break history) Mainframe System Operator Functions • Ensure that processes are followed to actively monitor mainframe online and batch operations; monitor and respond to WTO commands; monitor certain JES queues; vary failed drives offline; start / stop started tasks (per schedule and on request); reprioritize job class assignments for priority workloads; coordinate tests of contingency sites • Work with the application team staff during the development of new print forms; ensure that new / updated print forms are run through representative tests and meet FISA-OPA data center print standards (e.g., printed form dimensions, quality, restart capabilities, etc) • Execute projects to upgrade and / or reconfigure printer, cutter & un-winder equipment; coordinate periodic servicing, calibration and maintenance of the printer, cutter & un-winders; ensure that equipment is configured to provide redundancy for all critical print jobs • Under the direction of the Data Center Director: develop and monitor processes to log check print operations per audit requirements; perform root cause analysis on print equipment failures/errors (e.g., jams, bad cuts, etc.); create and update procedures for use of high-speed printers to accept jobs from Info print and mainframe print queues Mailing/Inserter Equipment Management • Ensure that new / updated mail items are run through representative tests and meet FISA-OPA mailing standards (e.g., dimensions and use of AIMS for quality control, alignment with envelope windows, etc); test AIMS software upgrades • Execute tasks for projects to upgrade and / or reconfigure inserter equipment; coordinate periodic servicing, calibration and maintenance of the inserters; ensure that equipment is configured to provide redundancy for all critical print jobs Management of Data Center Equipment and Print Workspaces • For work performed on the shift: escalate failure of infrastructure teams to abide by data center workspace policies; enforce procedures that ensure the print room and a clean / clutter free workspace; ensure that items to are discarded as appropriate for shredding; test print jobs are clearly labeled and / or discarded Quality Control for Check Print/Handling Functions • The individual will be expected to author and update procedures for quality control of check stock prior to printing; initial checks released to printer for alignment and first check imaged; end of the check run; storage of checks for handling in the morning; voided checks • The individual will be expected to author and update procedures for: use AIMS for reconciliation of expected print forms to inserted print forms; handling of print forms damaged during on auto-mailer; intake and counting of externally printed checks Distribution and Courier Management • Coordinate distribution operations with the FISA-OPA Mailroom; change adoption and sustainability, ensuring impacted stakeholders are prepared to transition to new processes, technologies, roles, and operating models. •	Serve as a central OCM point of coordination for LRP, connecting business, program, technology, vendor, and stakeholder groups to ensure change activities are integrated rather than managed independently. •	Provide hands-on project management leadership, maintaining schedules, action logs, deliverables, dependencies, status reporting, and follow-through across the OCM workstream.

This license must be maintained throughout the duration of the appointment in this position

The New York City Department of Design and Construction is seeking a college-level intern to support the Finance and Administration team within the Office of the Deputy Commissioner of IT, Data Analytics, and Project Controls. Reporting to the Director of Finance and Administration, the intern will provide administrative and analytical support across three focus areas: equipment and asset inventory management, policy and Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) documentation, and budget tracking. This is a hands-on opportunity for a student pursuing any field of study, with an interest in public service or local government, to gain direct exposure to how a NYC capital agency manages its internal operations, procurement pipeline, and budget process — working alongside the team's administrative and financial staff on real, ongoing work. The intern will work closely with the Finance and Administration team and will have the opportunity to build practical skills in public-sector budgeting, procurement, and data tools such as Excel and Airtable, with guidance and mentorship from experienced staff throughout the assignment. This role includes exposure to internal budget, procurement, and personnel-related records, which the intern will be expected to handle professionally. Responsibilities • Help build out and maintain the division's IT Asset Tracker, a hardware and equipment database covering laptops, desktops, tablets, and monitors — keeping device, staff assignment, and purchase order records current and accurate. • Support periodic reconciliation audits comparing tracked equipment against what's on hand and help resolve discrepancies. • Help track new hardware from purchase order through delivery and assignment to staff. • Assist in drafting and formatting new internal process documents — covering workflows such as onboarding/offboarding or procurement intake — using the team's established policy template and style. • Help keep the division's growing library of internal process documents organized and consistently formatted. • Assist with Personal Services / Other Than Personal Services (PS/OTPS) budget tracking spreadsheets, flagging variances for review. • Help organize and file internal budget and procurement backup documentation. • Assist with data entry and maintenance of administrative tracking systems, including the staff roster and HR action tracking. • Provide light research support (e.g., vendor or rate comparisons) and help prepare materials for internal team meetings. Additionally, educational credentials must be from a U.S. Department of Education-recognized accredited institution. Credentials from foreign institutions require independent equivalency verification from an approved evaluation service. A list of providers (fees apply) is available at: https://www.nyc.gov/assets/dcas/downloads/pdf/employment/nyc-dcas-foreign-education-evaluation-guide.pdf. All applicants, including City Employees: Please go to NYC Government Jobs Explore Careers City of New York, go to Search for Open Jobs, and type in the Job ID # listed above. Submit job application as prompted. Do not apply via Employee Self-Service (ESS), e-mail, mail, or fax your resume to DDC directly.
Requisitos: For Assignment Level I: Matriculation at an accredited college or graduate school. Employment is conditioned upon continuance as a student in a college or graduate school. For Assignment Level II (Information Technology): Matriculation at an accredited college or graduate school. Employment is conditioned upon continuance as a student in a college or graduate school with a specific course of study in information technology, computer science, management information systems, data processing, or closely related field, including or supplemented by 9 semester credits in an acceptable course of study. For Assignment Level III (Information Technology Fellow): Matriculation at an accredited college or graduate school. Employment is conditioned upon continuance as a student in a college or graduate school with a specific course of study in information technology, computer science, management information systems, data processing, or other area relevant to the information technology project(s) assigned, including or supplemented by 9 semester credits in an acceptable course of study. Appointments to this Assignment Level will be made by the Technology Steering Committee through the Department of Information Technology and Telecommunications. SPECIAL NOTE Maximum tenure for all Assignment Levels in the title of College Aide is 6 years. No student shall be employed more than half-time in any week in which classes in which the student is enrolled are in session. Students may be employed full-time during their vacation periods.
Habilidades: • Enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate program in any field of study, with an interest in public service, local government, or administrative operations. • Curiosity about databases and tracking tools like Airtable — no prior experience required; training provided. • Basic familiarity with Microsoft Excel and Word, with a willingness to build more advanced skills (formulas, pivot tables, etc.) on the job. • Willingness to learn new tools and processes, and comfort working with structured data and spreadsheets. • Comfortable asking questions and taking direction from supervising staff. • Developing written communication skills, with an interest in improving documentation and writing ability.

Laboratory activities include testing asphalt mixtures, reclaimed asphalt pavement (RAP), aggregates, asphalt binder, and other raw materials; evaluating materials for compliance with NYC DOT specifications and ASTM standards; and supporting research, development, and implementation of sustainable paving technologies. The Laboratory Technician maintains laboratory equipment and facilities, follows established safety and quality-control procedures, and assists with special assignments, research projects, emergency testing, and production-related investigations. The position requires effective communication and coordination with asphalt plant personnel, laboratory and engineering staff, Quality Control personnel, contractors, vendors, and other NYC DOT personnel. Titulo: Analytics & Reporting Engineer for the Division of Strategic Operations & Analytics
Descricao: About the Agency: The Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) oversees housing standards across all 3.7 million homes in New York City. As the nation’s largest municipal housing agency, HPD is responsible for building and preserving affordable housing, protecting tenants from harassment and displacement, and holding landlords accountable across the five boroughs. Under Commissioner Dina Levy and the Mamdani Administration, HPD is pursuing an ambitious housing agenda focused on the needs of New York’s tenants. With a broad set of tools including standards enforcement, tenant resources, and the creation of new affordable housing, HPD is committed to making New York City a more affordable place for renters and homeowners alike. Your Team: The Office of Policy and Strategy (OPS) leverage its expertise to guide and support HPD and its many Offices in their efforts to deepen their impact, optimize their efficiency, and become more data-driven, climate-adaptive, and mission-focused. As part of OPS, the Division of Strategic Operations and Analytics (SOA) works to increase HPD's impact by analyzing and improving operations agency-wide. SOA does this by clarifying HPD program missions, objectives, and stakeholders; implementing initiatives that advance HPD's goals; analyzing data to deliver actionable insights to HPD programs; and increasing the agency's overall ability to leverage data. Your Impact: As the Analytics & Reporting Engineer within SOA, you will play a key role in making HPD’s data more accessible, reliable, and reusable to support reporting and analytics. By building well-structured datasets, automations and data flows, you will help SOA and other HPD offices turn data into key reporting and metrics that support key agency programs for New Yorkers. Your Role: Your role will focus on hands-on development of data pipelines, curating datasets and data flows in SQL Server and building reusable scripts and code to support reporting and analytics work for agency programs such as homeless placement services, homebuyer assistance, housing distress & compliance, and fair housing work. You will also create and maintain reports and dashboards, or related dataflows/models. Exercising independent judgement and initiative, you will implement solutions through scalable data models, automated workflows, and well-structured datasets and BI data flows - to enable more efficient reporting, research, and analytics for key agency programs. Your Responsibilities: •	Build and maintain core datasets, data models, and dashboards to support key program reporting and analytics •	Build and automate Python-based data cleaning and integration pipelines — merging data across siloed source systems and using automation tools — to support reporting needs for housing placements, fair housing and more. •	Load cleaned datasets into SQL Server and connect to BI tools (e.g. Power BI) to support reporting/dashboarding. •	Implement basic code validation, testing, and documentation practices to keep analytics scripts and datasets reliable and maintainable. •	Document code standards and workflows so datasets and scripts remain usable/maintainable by the team over time. •	Apply data engineering skills and creative collaboration techniques to address technical issues and drive the approach for the team Preferred skills •	Inquisitive, self-motivated problem-solver who is passionate about making organizations more data-driven •	Comfortable working in a fast-moving, resource-constrained environment with messy data and legacy systems; motivated by rolling up your sleeves and building practical tools that make a real impact on people's lives. •	Experience building or supporting data pipelines (ETL/ELT) — extracting, cleaning, and transforming data from multiple sources. •	Experience working with relational databases (e.g., SQL Server or similar) •	Some experience with BI data modeling (preferably Power BI or similar) is a plus •	Familiarity with source control and version control workflows (e.g., Azure DevOps Repos) •	Strong interpersonal and organizational skills; able to ask thoughtful questions and collaborate across teams •	Strong aptitude for learning new tools and technologies independently using online resources •	Technical skills: SQL, Python, Power BI data modeling (DAX, Power Query M), and data modeling fundamentals
Requisitos: 1. To be appointed to Assignment Level II and above, candidates must have: 1. A doctorate degree from an accredited college or university with specialization in an appropriate field of physical, biological, environmental or social science and one year of full-time experience in a responsible supervisory, administrative or research capacity in the appropriate field of specialization; or 2. A master's degree from an accredited college or university with specialization in an appropriate field of physical, biological, environmental or social science and three years of responsible full-time research experience in the appropriate field of specialization; or 3. Education and/or experience which is equivalent to "1" or "2" above. However, all candidates must have at least a master's degree in an appropriate field of specialization and at least two years of experience described in "2" above. Two years as a City Research Scientist Level I can be substituted for the experience required in "1" and "2" above. Titulo: Senior Manager of Cyber Security Operations
Descricao: The New York City Housing Authority (NYCHA), the largest public housing authority in North America, provides decent, affordable housing for low- and moderate-income New Yorkers. NYCHA is home to 1 in 17 New Yorkers, providing affordable housing to over 500,000 authorized residents through public housing and Permanent Affordability Commitment Together (PACT) programs as well as Section 8 housing. NYCHA has nearly 200,000 apartments in over 2,400 buildings across 335 conventional public housing and PACT developments. In addition, NYCHA connects residents to critical programs and services from external and internal partners, with a focus on economic opportunity, youth, seniors, and social services. With a housing stock that spans all five boroughs, NYCHA is a city within a city. Under direction of the Chief information Security Officer, with wide latitude for independent initiative and judgement, NYCHA is looking for an experienced manager to lead its Security Operations Center (SOC) and take it to the next level. This role is about more than keeping the lights on: the Senior Manager will mature the SOC's detection and response capabilities, drive automation to make the team faster and more consistent, and prepare NYCHA for a threat landscape increasingly shaped by artificial intelligence, both by defending against AI-enabled attacks and by putting AI to work in security operations. This individual owns every security incident from detection through resolution, evaluating and assessing each event, directing the response, and keeping senior leadership informed with clear, timely updates. The ideal candidate brings hands-on experience in incident response and detection engineering, stays calm under pressure, and is a proven leader who develops their analysts and builds a collaborative team. The selected candidate will lead a team of three security analysts and report directly to the Chief Information Security Officer. If you are a seasoned cybersecurity professional with a passion for safeguarding critical infrastructure and a commitment to public service, we encourage you to apply and become a part of NYCHA's mission. Roles and Responsibilities •	Team Leadership: Mentor and develop SOC analysts, assign work based on skills and experience, set goals, evaluate performance, and participate in hiring as the team grows. •	SOC Operations: Direct the day-to-day operations of the SOC, including monitoring, alert triage, investigation, and escalation, and lead the response to all security incidents from detection through recovery. Assess current SOC capabilities and maintain a roadmap to mature them, tracking progress through metrics such as mean time to detect and respond. •	Leadership Communication: Provide clear and timely incident updates to senior leadership and support required regulatory and oversight reporting. •	Readiness and Continuous Improvement: Maintain incident response playbooks and procedures, run tabletop exercises, and lead post-incident reviews to identify root causes and drive changes that prevent recurrence. •	Detection Engineering and Threat Hunting: Oversee the development and tuning of detection rules, guide proactive threat hunting informed by threat intelligence, and keep detections current with evolving attacker techniques, including AI-enabled threats automate triage, enrichment, and response actions to improve speed and consistency. •	Collaboration with IT: Work closely with IT infrastructure, application, and service desk teams to investigate and remediate security events and to ensure monitoring is built into new systems. Additional Information 1.	NYCHA employees applying for transfer, promotional, title or level change opportunities must have served a period of one year at current location and in current title and level (if applicable). 2.	NYCHA residents are encouraged to apply. 3.	NYCHA provides benefits that include a choice of medical coverage plans, deferred compensation plans and a defined pension benefit plan as a member of the New York City Employees’ Retirement System (NYCERS). Please read this posting carefully to make certain you meet the minimum qualification requirements before applying to this position.
Requisitos: A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college and four years of satisfactory full-time experience related to projects and policies required by the particular position; or, Education and/or experience which is equivalent to "1" above.
Habilidades: •	Security Information and Event Management (SIEM): In-depth knowledge of Splunk or equivalent SIEM platforms for real-time monitoring, log analysis, and threat detection, with the ability to design effective searches, alerts, dashboards, and reports. •	Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR): Proficiency in using CrowdStrike Falcon or similar EDR solutions to detect, investigate, contain, and remediate threats on endpoints. •	Incident Response and Forensics: Extensive hands-on experience leading incident response, including evidence collection, host and network forensics, malware triage, and root cause analysis. •	Threat Detection and Hunting: Strong working knowledge of the MITRE ATT&CK framework and hands-on experience building detections and conducting hunts mapped to attacker tactics and techniques. •	AI in Security Operations: Experience applying AI and machine learning capabilities to alert triage, investigation, and response, with an understanding of their limitations and risks. •	Monitoring and Investigation: Experience monitoring and investigating activity across network, identity, email, cloud, and data protection. •	Automation and Scripting: Ability to use scripting languages (such as PowerShell, Python, or Bash) and security orchestration tools to automate SOC tasks and streamline incident response. •	Regulatory Compliance: Understanding of industry standards (e.g., NIST CSF, NIST SP 800-61, ISO 27001) and experience with incident reporting obligations in a public-sector or regulated environment. •	Able to be in the office three days per week and part of a hybrid work environment.
